Act as the implementation sub-agent for this task.

Fix GitHub issue #17 in repo gemini-4-braincells (product "Shill or Chill", a Bluesky coordinated-amplification detector). Deadline is tight; keep the change minimal. Worktree starts at origin/main 4ac5d81. Read `.entire/agent-guide.md` first and use `entire graph query/def/neighbors/impact --repo . --head ...` to find code and callers (not grep).

Issue (`gh issue view 17`): word counts use whitespace splitting, so unspaced scripts (Japanese, Chinese, Thai) never reach thresholds:
```python
from signals.textnorm import normalize_text, tokens
t = '今日は東京で大雨が降っていて電車が止まっています。みんな気をつけてください。'
len(tokens(normalize_text(t)))          # 2  (needs min_text_tokens=5)
from sources.links import claim_phrase
claim_phrase([t])                       # None
```
Effects: Japanese/Chinese/Thai copy-paste campaigns get no `duplicate_text` / `near_duplicate_text` key (`signals/keys.py`), and POST /api/analyze answers 'Text too short ... (needs 5+ words)' for a long Japanese sentence. Japanese is ~4% of posts.

Files: `signals/textnorm.py` (`normalize_text`, `tokens`, `text_hash`), `signals/keys.py` (min_text_tokens / shingles for near-duplicates; check `signals/config.py` for the thresholds), `sources/links.py` (`claim_phrase`, `_SENTENCE_SPLIT`). Run `entire graph impact --repo . --head --symbol tokens` and for `claim_phrase` first: `tokens` also feeds similarity elsewhere in signals/ (and ingest uses textnorm for text_hash — text_hash must NOT change, it is stored in the DB). Note `lookup/textsim.py` has its own separate `tokens`; leave it alone unless trivially needed.

Suggested approach (you decide, but keep it small): treat runs of CJK ideographs / Hiragana / Katakana / Hangul-without-spaces / Thai as character-based: e.g. in `tokens()`, split such runs into single characters or character bigrams so that length thresholds and shingles work, while space-separated scripts are unchanged byte-for-byte. Make the effective minimum for unspaced text comparable to 5 words (e.g. ~10 characters), so short greetings ('おはようございます') don't become content keys. For `claim_phrase`: also split sentences on 。！？ and for unspaced text use a character length (e.g. min 10, max ~30 characters) instead of words. The API note text in `api/routes/analyze.py` ('needs 5+ words') is being edited by another agent in parallel — do NOT edit `api/routes/analyze.py`; if its note wording should change, say so in your final reply with the exact suggested string.

THIS IS A DETECTOR CHANGE. Prod publishes recall/FPR from this detector. Rules:
1. Do not bump `signals/config.py VERSION` (a parallel PR #38 by Kirill bumps it to v1.7; the orchestrator sets the version at merge). Don't touch `organic_guards` in `signals/score.py` (other agents edit it).
2. Baseline evals on unchanged origin/main are already running/written by the orchestrator into `/tmp/claude-1001/-home-dev--t3-worktrees-gemini-4-braincells-dev-rehearsal-fixes-e7e6b1c65348029b/a6f19541-74c1-4cee-8c6c-24697dc3506b/scratchpad/evals/baseline/` (files organic-{heldout,dev}.{json,txt}, recall-{heldout,dev}.{json,txt}; a file DONE appears when finished). Do not re-run the baseline. After your change, run the SAME evals on your worktree with the script: `/tmp/claude-1001/-home-dev--t3-worktrees-gemini-4-braincells-dev-rehearsal-fixes-e7e6b1c65348029b/a6f19541-74c1-4cee-8c6c-24697dc3506b/scratchpad/evals/run.sh <your worktree abs path> cjk` (writes to .../scratchpad/evals/cjk/, runs organic heldout+dev offline and recall heldout+dev with live base rates; takes a while — the server is loaded, run it in the background and wait for evals/cjk/DONE). You may first do a quick smoke run on fewer windows (`--max-windows`), but the reported delta must come from the full run. Never pass --write or --database-url.
3. Compare after vs baseline: organic_synth and organic_live FPR (heldout and dev, incl. fpr_given_clustered and counts), recall overall and per level. Produce a short delta table. If held-out FPR (organic_synth or organic_live heldout) goes UP, do not open the PR as ready: make it a draft, report why, and propose a tighter variant (or none).
4. Regression tests in `tests/test_signals.py` (and `tests/test_sources_checker.py` for claim_phrase): the Japanese example above yields >=5 tokens / a content key when 5+ accounts post it; a short Japanese greeting does not; space-separated text tokens and `text_hash` unchanged (assert a few known values computed BEFORE your change); claim_phrase returns a Japanese phrase for the example and None for a short one; a Thai example too.

Verify: `uv run pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider` must pass except the one known pre-existing failure `tests/test_media_path.py::test_stored_media_reaches_api_and_dashboard` (fixed separately). ruff check/format on changed files if configured.

Then branch `dev/cjk-text-keys`, commit (end commit message with `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`), push, open a PR with `gh pr create` titled "signals: CJK/Thai text gets content keys and a web-search phrase (#17)"; body: what/why, the eval delta table (before = origin/main 4ac5d81, after = your head), tests, "Refs #17" (not "Fixes"), ending with "🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)". Add a line to `signals/README.md` only if it documents tokenisation. If push fails on unreadable Entire objects, push from a fresh clone: `git clone --single-branch --branch main https://github.com/JustinasLa/gemini-4-braincells.git ~/work/cjk-push && cd ~/work/cjk-push && git fetch <worktree> dev/cjk-text-keys:dev/cjk-text-keys && git push -u origin dev/cjk-text-keys`. Do NOT merge. Don't deploy. Never copy files from /srv/junction-espoo/plan/ into git; never print secrets/.env.

Final reply: PR URL, head SHA, eval delta table, tests added, pytest line, suggested analyze note wording.

"""Text and URL normalisation shared by ingest (text_hash, embed_urls) and signals (similarity).

Kept dependency-free and deterministic: the same input always gives the same output.
"""

import hashlib
import re
import unicodedata
from urllib.parse import parse_qsl, urlencode, urlsplit, urlunsplit

_URL_RE = re.compile(r"(?:https?://|www\.)\S+", re.IGNORECASE)
_BARE_DOMAIN_RE = re.compile(r"\b[a-z0-9-]+(?:\.[a-z0-9-]+)*\.[a-z]{2,}(?:/\S*)?", re.IGNORECASE)
_MENTION_RE = re.compile(r"@[\w.-]+")
_NON_WORD_RE = re.compile(r"[^\w#]+", re.UNICODE)
_WS_RE = re.compile(r"\s+")
_SCHEME_RE = re.compile(r"^[a-z][a-z0-9+.-]*:(?!\d)", re.IGNORECASE)

# Query parameters that only track clicks; dropping them makes the same link compare equal.
_TRACKING_PARAMS = {
    "fbclid",
    "gclid",
    "dclid",
    "msclkid",
    "igshid",
    "mc_cid",
    "mc_eid",
    "_ga",
    "_gl",
    "ref",
    "ref_src",
    "ref_url",
    "si",
    "feature",
    "share",
    "s",
    "t",
    "smid",
    "cmpid",
    "yclid",
    "twclid",
    "ttclid",
    "spm",
    "src",
    "via",
}


def normalize_text(text: str | None) -> str:
    """Lowercase, NFKC, strip URLs, @mentions, emoji and punctuation; keep words and #tags."""
    if not text:
        return ""
    t = unicodedata.normalize("NFKC", text).lower()
    t = _URL_RE.sub(" ", t)
    t = _BARE_DOMAIN_RE.sub(" ", t)
    t = _MENTION_RE.sub(" ", t)
    t = _NON_WORD_RE.sub(" ", t)  # emoji, punctuation, symbols
    t = t.replace("_", " ")
    return _WS_RE.sub(" ", t).strip()


def tokens(norm_text: str) -> list[str]:
    return norm_text.split() if norm_text else []


def text_hash(text: str | None) -> str | None:
    """Stable 16-hex hash of the normalised text, or None when nothing is left after normalising."""
    norm = normalize_text(text)
    if not norm:
        return None
    return hashlib.blake2b(norm.encode(), digest_size=8).hexdigest()


MAX_URL_LEN = 1000  # Postgres index entries max out near 2.7 kB; real links are far shorter


def normalize_url(url: str | None) -> str | None:
    """Canonical form for comparing links: https, lowercase host without www., no fragment,
    no tracking params, sorted query, no trailing slash. Resolves nothing (no network)."""
    if not url:
        return None
    url = url.strip()
    if not url:
        return None
    if "://" not in url:
        if _SCHEME_RE.match(url):  # mailto:, javascript:, data: ...
            return None
        url = "https://" + url
    try:
        parts = urlsplit(url)
    except ValueError:
        return None
    if parts.scheme.lower() not in ("http", "https"):
        return None
    host = (parts.hostname or "").lower().rstrip(".")
    if not host:
        return None
    if host.startswith("www."):
        host = host[4:]
    try:
        port = parts.port
    except ValueError:
        return None
    if port and port not in (80, 443):
        host = f"{host}:{port}"
    query = [
        (k, v)
        for k, v in parse_qsl(parts.query, keep_blank_values=True)
        if not k.lower().startswith("utm_") and k.lower() not in _TRACKING_PARAMS
    ]
    query.sort()
    path = parts.path or ""
    if path.endswith("/"):
        path = path.rstrip("/")
    out = urlunsplit(("https", host, path, urlencode(query), ""))
    return out[:MAX_URL_LEN]


def url_domain(normalized_url: str) -> str:
    """Host part of a normalised URL (e.g. 'example.com')."""
    return urlsplit(normalized_url).hostname or ""
"""Pure helpers: which links a cluster shares, and which phrase to search the web for."""

import re
from collections import Counter
from collections.abc import Iterable
from urllib.parse import urlsplit

from signals.textnorm import normalize_url
from sources.models import ClusterPost

# Links that point back into Bluesky itself say nothing about outside sources.
SKIP_HOSTS = frozenset({"bsky.app", "go.bsky.app"})
MEDIA_SUFFIXES = (".jpg", ".jpeg", ".png", ".gif", ".webp", ".mp4", ".mov", ".m3u8")

_URL = re.compile(r"https?://\S+")
_MENTION_OR_TAG = re.compile(r"(?<!\w)[@#][\w.\-]+")
_SENTENCE_SPLIT = re.compile(r"(?<=[.!?])\s+|\n+")


def checkable_url(url: str) -> str | None:
    """The canonical URL (same form ingest stores) if it is worth a source check, else None."""
    norm = normalize_url(url)
    if not norm:
        return None
    parts = urlsplit(norm)
    host = parts.hostname or ""
    if host in SKIP_HOSTS or host == "localhost" or re.fullmatch(r"[\d.:]+", host):
        return None
    if parts.path.lower().endswith(MEDIA_SUFFIXES):
        return None
    return norm


def domain(url: str) -> str:
    return (urlsplit(url).hostname or "").lower().removeprefix("www.")


def top_links(posts: Iterable[ClusterPost], k: int) -> list[tuple[str, int]]:
    """The k links shared by the most distinct accounts: [(normalized_url, n_accounts)]."""
    sharers: dict[str, set[str]] = {}
    for p in posts:
        for raw in p.embed_urls:
            url = checkable_url(raw)
            if url:
                sharers.setdefault(url, set()).add(p.did)
    ranked = sorted(sharers.items(), key=lambda kv: (-len(kv[1]), kv[0]))
    return [(url, len(dids)) for url, dids in ranked[:k]]


def _clean(text: str) -> str:
    text = _MENTION_OR_TAG.sub(" ", _URL.sub(" ", text))
    return re.sub(r"[ \t]+", " ", text).strip()


def claim_phrase(
    texts: Iterable[str | None], *, min_words: int = 5, max_words: int = 12
) -> str | None:
    """A distinctive phrase from the cluster's most repeated text, for an exact-phrase search.

    Takes the longest sentence of the most common (cleaned) text and cuts it to `max_words`.
    None when no sentence has at least `min_words` words: short phrases match too much of the web.
    """
    cleaned = [c for c in (_clean(t) for t in texts if t) if c]
    if not cleaned:
        return None
    common, _ = Counter(c.lower() for c in cleaned).most_common(1)[0]
    original = next(c for c in cleaned if c.lower() == common)
    sentences = [s.strip(" \"'“”") for s in _SENTENCE_SPLIT.split(original)]
    best = max(sentences, key=lambda s: len(s.split()), default="")
    words = best.split()
    if len(words) < min_words:
        return None
    return " ".join(words[:max_words]).rstrip(",;:")
